summary: A horizontal slider: dragging or tapping the track sets its variable between min and max (the thumb jumps under the finger and follows it); it can show the value at its end, and onRelease runs actions with the released level (a host action sends it to the app). A screen reader hears the label and the current value.

value.doc: The value, kept in min..max. Bind a document variable ("@volume") to preset it and read it after the slider; omitted, the slider keeps its own. A drag writes the slider's OWN variable ("@volume" read after the slider is the live value); the bound variable itself (a resources variable, exported or not) is written only on release, and only when onRelease is given. To hand the level to the app, bind it and send it from onRelease: {"onRelease": {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "setVolume", "value": "@volume", "valueType": "float"}}

min.doc: Value at the left end of the track

max.doc: Value at the right end of the track

label.doc: Accessibility label (the slider draws no title): put the visible name next to it and pass the same words

showValue.doc: Print the value at the right end (the track gets 48 dp shorter)

decimals.doc: Digits after the point in the printed value

onRelease.doc: Actions run when the finger lifts after a drag or a tap (onTouchUp on the track). Before them the slider writes the released level into the bound variable, so an action that reads it gets the new value: {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "setVolume", "value": "@volume", "valueType": "float"} sends it to the app (valueType is a json2rc extension: the Java parser writes only a literal value), and an exported variable is updated too. Name the variable you bound to `value`, not "@value" (a param name, not substituted inside actions); an unbound slider's level cannot be named. Omitted: nothing runs on release and the bytes are unchanged

pitfalls: The drag is a touchExpression in absolute mode (touchMode 6) named after the bound variable: from the slider on, "@volume" is the touch value (it starts at the variable's own value and keeps where the finger left it). Read the value AFTER the slider in the document: the parsers bind names in document order, so a text placed before it, or an expression in resources, keeps reading the starting value

onRelease: the canvas carries two onTouchUp modifiers, which come BEFORE the touchExpression in the document, so there "@volume" still names the bound (resources) variable, not the touch value. The first modifier therefore recomputes the level from where the finger lifted (valueFloatExpressionChange: clamp(min, max, the touch expression's own formula)) into the bound variable; the second runs the caller's actions, which read it. A plain tap ends the same way. About 120 B per call with one host action (measured: 1040 -> 1162 B)
touchX() is in document coordinates, so the slider measures where it sits (componentValue POS_ROOT_X into a local) and subtracts it: it works anywhere in the layout, scrolled or padded

Players that predate the T31-T33 / C49-C50 fixes (2026-10-30) map the drag wrong: the TS player read 0 for POS_ROOT_X and let every slider take every touch, and the C++ player hit-tested a nested touch expression in its own coordinates. Java, and the TS and C++ players from that date, put the value under the finger
The value is continuous: there are no steps (the notch stop modes need touchSpec, which the Java parser ignores, U8). Round where you read it (textFromFloat decimals, floor())
It fills the width it is given (fillMaxWidth) and is 40 dp tall: in a row, give it a weight or a box with a width
No easing on the value: the thumb follows the finger frame for frame (an animated value would trail it). In mono it looks the same, a thin grey track, a thicker white active part and a smaller thumb

Accessibility: a transparent box over the track carries the label and the value as its state (textFromFloat of the live value: `decimals` digits, at least 2 when max - min is under 1.5, so 0..1 reads 0.7, not 0). It comes after the canvas because only from the touchExpression on does the name read the dragged value; it takes no touch, so the drag still works. No role (the JSON semantics has no role key), and no adjust actions: a screen reader announces the value but cannot step it. About 85 B per call
